title: Threat Actors Use Claude Code, Codex and DeepSeek AI to Power Cyberattacks
content_md: A new threat intelligence report from Gambit Security has documented a ransomware affiliate using generative AI as an operational partner throughout a live intrusion campaign, highlighting how AI-assisted attacks are moving far beyond phishing content and basic malware generation. Nir Varon said a suspected affiliate of the Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service operation used Anthropic’s Claude Code to support nearly every phase of compromise. The activity reportedly included targeting internet-exposed VPN appliances, harvesting credentials, enumerating Active Directory infrastructure, modifying firewall settings, and staging SQL database backups for exfiltration. Threat Actors Use Claude Code, Codex and DeepSeek AI The operator allegedly relied on Claude Sonnet 4.6, a less-restricted model version that may have offered fewer safety controls than newer frontier AI systems. Gambit assessed that the actor compromised at least eight organizations across several sectors, including an Australian energy utility, a Mauritius-based financial-services firm, manufacturing companies in Thailand and the United States, and IT and distribution organizations. Attribution to The Gentlemen RaaS was rated medium confidence. The assessment was based on overlap with the group’s leak site, infrastructure links identified by Hunt.io, and the intruder’s recurring focus on backup systems, an objective commonly associated with ransomware operators seeking to prevent recovery before extortion.
